rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Never interpolate a credential variable with ${VAR:-fallback} in a liveness check; the :- form expands to the SECRET when set. Use ${VAR:+set}, and treat any command that names a token variable as a publishing action RECURRENCE of FM-96, 2026-08-15 14:12 EDT, committed by an agent that had FM-96 loaded in its context at the time. Checking GitHub auth before a push, the agent ran echo "GH_TOKEN: ${GH_TOKEN:+set}${GH_TOKEN:-UNSET}" intending to print set/UNSET. ${GH_TOKEN:-UNSET} expands to the VALUE when the variable is set, so the full ghs_ App installation token was printed to the transcript. The two idioms differ by one character and read identically at a glance. Evidence that a preloaded CRITICAL warning does not prevent the failure it describes: the entry was in-context and the operator was actively working ON the failure-mode registry. Audit triggered by this leak found 62 distinct ghs_ App tokens plus 5 distinct full-length long-lived credentials (2 gho_, 3 ghp_) across 14 transcript files dated 2026-07-23..2026-08-10; all full-length values scrubbed 2026-08-15, no rotation performed (founder decision, assumed dead). Mechanizable check: forbid the :- and :? forms on any variable whose name matches (TOKEN|SECRET|KEY|PASSWORD|CREDENTIAL), and grep persisted transcripts for gh[pous]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36} as a post-session assertion.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Branch-name shape shadows binding identity in task resolution cmd_land routed task resolution on whether a PR head branch's NAME matched a project convention (dispatch/<task>) before checking lane-binding identity (managed_branch/pr_number). A --continue-pr lane whose external destination coincidentally matched that naming shape got misrouted into legacy logic and wrongly refused, even though its binding was valid and delivered. Caught by independent pev review despite a fully green (181/181) acceptance suite. Fix (fleet#405/PR#539): always resolve by binding identity first, fall back to name-shape heuristics only when identity resolution finds nothing.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Direct exit on a mid-flow refusal bypasses terminal-state machinery, stranding the lane In cli-dispatch's _cmd_start, a --continue-pr lane's destination_deliver() refusal (e.g. a foreign actor moving the PR's destination ref mid-run) caused the code to exit directly, bypassing the classify_terminal_state ladder and the delivered-transition -- the only two places that ever advance run_state/binding state out of running/active. destination_deliver() itself never transitions the binding on a refusal either. Result: a lane whose delivery failed after a successful managed-branch push was stranded forever with run_state=running, binding state=active. Fix (fleet#405/PR#539): write a terminal run_state and transition the binding to aborted before exiting on this path. General lesson: any early-exit added on a new failure path must be checked against whether it bypasses existing state-machine invariants, not just checked for the right exit code.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: New exclusion whitelist for a resource lookup had zero test coverage lane_binding_lookup_task_by_pr's state whitelist (provisioning/active/delivered/landed) exists specifically to exclude aborted/provisioning-failed lane bindings from PR-number-keyed resolution -- a stale/aborted binding sharing a pr_number with a live one must never hijack land --pr's task resolution. This exclusion had zero test coverage: confirmed by mutation, dropping the whitelist entirely left the PR's own 21-case acceptance suite unchanged, 21/21 passing. Fix (fleet#405/PR#539): added a regression test reusing an existing abort fixture. General lesson: an added guard clause needs a test asserting the guard specifically, not just that the happy path still works -- a suite can be fully green while a real invariant has zero coverage.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: pev's per-round review agents are all pinned to the same model as the coordinator, defeating cross-vendor independence ~/.claude/workflows/pev.js pins model:'sonnet' on every stage (ground truth, lenses, adjudicate) with no vendor variation. Across 6 rounds of pev review on fleet PR #539, both the fix author (the coordinating Claude Sonnet session) and every reviewing agent were the same model family -- N reviewers in one vendor is not independent review per the standing 'Claude is QA, Codex builds' / cross-vendor-review-routing policy, even though the 6 rounds were genuinely separate dispatched contexts (so not literally N=1 by the convergence-is-not-corroboration family, but still same-vendor throughout). Caught only because the founder asked directly what had been forgotten; nothing in the pipeline itself flagged the gap. A follow-up genuine cross-vendor (Codex) audit of the merged code found 2 additional real bugs pev's 6 same-vendor rounds missed (fleet#542: --onto never wired to destination_deliver(), a pre-existing gap from #403/#404 that #405 didn't close; fleet#543: the round-2 stranded-lane fix's own abort-transition swallows its failure with || true). Fix: pev.js (or its caller) should pin at least one stage per round to a non-Claude model when the PR being reviewed was itself Claude-authored, mirroring the model-override pattern already used for the ground/lenses stages -- or the coordinator must explicitly dispatch a separate cross-vendor pass via cli-dispatch before merge, not rely on pev alone, whenever it personally wrote the fix under review.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Abort-path bookkeeping failure swallowed with || true, re-stranding the resource it was meant to protect fleet cli-dispatch's --continue-pr delivery-refusal handler calls lane_binding_transition(...) aborted || true before exit -- if the transition write itself fails, the || true discards that failure silently and the lane can be left in a non-terminal state exactly like the bug it was written to fix (fleet#405 round 2). This is the abort-path-is-load-bearing pattern: repairing an error path to 'do the right thing' still needs its own success to be checked, or the repair is cosmetic. Fix: check the transition's own exit status and escalate/log distinctly if it fails, rather than exit-swallowing a second layer deep.

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: A shared safety function (destination_deliver) wired for only one of two production callers, leaving the other silently unverified cli-dispatch's destination_deliver() -- the fail-closed function that pushes to a bound destination ref and verifies exact old-OID + fast-forward -- is gated at its only call site by [[ "$pushed" == "true" && -n "$continue_pr" && -n "$lane_id" ]]. The -n "$continue_pr" condition means start --onto NEVER reaches this block, even though --onto also sets a binding_destination and claims the same delivered-state guarantee. An --onto lane can report state=delivered while its destination ref was never pushed to, verified, or divergence-checked. destination_deliver() was added by fleet#404 explicitly 'dormant until #403' pending a caller wiring it up; fleet#405 wired it for --continue-pr only and never revisited --onto, and none of 6 same-vendor pev review rounds on #405 caught the gap in the sibling mode -- a genuine cross-vendor (Codex) audit did. General lesson: when a shared safety primitive is deliberately left dormant pending caller wiring, closing the loop for ONE caller does not retire the TODO -- grep all callers of the function/flag the primitive gates on before declaring the feature done, or the primitive's own docstring/comment should list every caller it must eventually cover.

rationale: filed at creation time

rationale: filed at creation time
evidence: Harness credential inherited at spawn, never re-synced (6th recurrence; recurrence of hc-FM-232) Long-lived non-interactive processes capture the GitHub App credential in their environment at spawn and hold it past its 1-hour TTL, while a freshly refreshed one sits in the on-disk cache beside them. The refresh hook rides on PROMPT_COMMAND, which is interactive-only, so background jobs, cron, and dispatched subagents never pick it up. Compounded twice: cron has no BASH_ENV so it inherits nothing at all, and cli-dispatch:5931 ADVISES falling back to a different identity on 401, encoding the violation in tooling. Measured 2026-08-15: the personal OAuth quota was driven to 0/5000 and re-drained to 0 within minutes of reset while the App pool sat at 7395/7500 unused. Downstream blast radius: starved lens agents returned null, which a vacuous merge gate (FM-285) then treated as unanimous PASS, so one dead credential produced unsound merges. Detection: check the rate-limit LIMIT, not the remaining (7500=App, 5000=OAuth); a 5000 in a session that believes it is on the App is proof it is not. Fix must be mechanical, not procedural: this is the 6th occurrence (2026-07-29, 07-30 x3, 08-10, 08-15) with a 100 percent miss rate for background sessions, and every prior occurrence closed by restating the rule. Fix the acquisition path and delete the advised fallback; per-harness refresh timers must exist for ALL harnesses (grok had none until 2026-08-15).
